posts.text: Over the past week, I’ve been overwhelmed by the love and support of friends, industry colleagues, and people I've never met. Thank you to everyone who has shown kindness to my family and me. It means the world to me. I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life. NVIDIA has been my life’s work. Building it into the company it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honor. Nowhere but in America could a company like NVIDIA be possible. I love our country, and I love NVIDIA. I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation. Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company. If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO. Thank you again to everyone who has shared their good wishes. I am profoundly humbled by your support. To my family: I love you, and I will spend the rest of my life being worthy of yours. Jensen

posts.author: bgurley
posts.text: It is critically important that everyone thinking about AI become familiar with the term “handoverism.” Many in the AI community believe that humanity should—or inevitably will—hand control of the world over to AI itself. Some view this not as a risk to be avoided, but as an outcome to be welcomed. Are we actually designing toward this future? This worldview is particularly relevant at Anthropic. Co-founder Tom Brown said: “There’s going to be a handoff where humanity will hand off control to transformative AI at some point.” In his seminal essay, Machines of Loving Grace, CEO Dario Amodei contemplates: “It could be a capitalist economy of AI systems, which then give out resources (huge amounts of them, since the overall economic pie will be gigantic) to humans based on some secondary economy of what the AI systems think makes sense to reward in humans (based on some judgment ultimately derived from human values).” Are you prepared to receive your “resources” from an AI system, based on criteria it determines? The full title of the poem Dario borrowed the title from is "All Watched Over by Machines of Loving Grace." Do you want to be "watched over" by AI? If Anthropic's founders believe that the ultimate destination is the transfer of human control to AI, the world deserves to know. Washington, D.C. deserves to know. American citizens deserve to know. And if that belief informs Anthropic's corporate objectives, it belongs in the Risk Factors section of its S-1. It isn't there today. I am decidedly anti-handoverism. I'm not here to tell you what your view should be. But I believe anyone making consequential decisions about AI—especially those drafting, advocating for, or enacting AI regulation—should be required to disclose where they stand on this fundamental question. A wonderfully thoughtful piece on the subject by @RuxandraTeslo: https://t.co/9rdlBoNX5j
